s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with transient atrioventricular block and ventricular asystole
salient_findings: Gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction
key_facts: No history of structural heart disease
No history of hypertension, myocarditis, or sleep apnea syndrome
No family history of cardiovascular disease and sudden death
Holter monitor recording showed ventricular asystole during syncope
Electrophysiologic studies showed no abnormalities in the cardiac conduction system

raw.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with transient atrioventricular block and ventricular asystole
salient_findings: Gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction
key_facts: No history of structural heart disease
No history of hypertension, myocarditis, or sleep apnea syndrome
No family history of cardiovascular disease and sudden death
Holter monitor recording showed ventricular asystole during syncope
Electrophysiologic studies showed no abnormalities in the cardiac conduction system

raw.rationale: The Holter monitor recording showed a 23.8-second ventricular asystole during syncope with gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction followed by complete atrioventricular block, which directly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: av block
rejected.why: Too general, as the specific type of block is identified as complete atrioventricular block.

rejected.label: congenital complete atrioventricular block
rejected.why: There is no indication that the condition is congenital, given the patient's age and lack of prior history.

rejected.label: arrhythmia
rejected.why: Too broad, as the specific arrhythmia is identified as complete atrioventricular block leading to asystole.

rejected.label: asystole
rejected.why: While asystole is present, it is a result of the complete atrioventricular block, making the block the primary diagnosis.
